To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the side-effect profile of CETP inhibitors can be rationalized by their off-target protein interactions and that combinatorial off-target interactions might be used as a strategy to minimize side effects of drugs.
we have identified a protein-ligand interaction network that can explain the side effect of CETP inhibitor, and that this approach can be applied to other drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new computational approach that can be used in the identification of the protein-ligand interaction network.

the development of novel computational methods to systematically identify the protein-ligand interaction network of drugs and to elucidate the complex modes of drug actions in a systems biology context.

the development and application of a novel computational approach to the identification of protein-ligand interactions on a genome-wide level, with the aim to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the adverse drug effects associated with a new class of cardiovascular therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the side effects of CETP inhibitors are modulated via combinatorial control exerted by a network of off-target proteins.
our study has identified a panel of potential off-targets of CETP inhibitors, which are associated with the side effects.
we have developed a novel computational strategy, termed chemical systems biology, to identify the protein-ligand interaction network that explains the side effects of CETP inhibitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the side effects of Torcetrapibs are caused by the off-targets that are involved in the regulation of blood pressure and the off-targets are identified through the combination of chemical systems biology and chemogenomics.
the protein-ligand networks are useful for understanding the side effects and the mechanisms of CETP inhibitors.
we have developed a new computational strategy to identify the protein-ligand interaction network for a given ligand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combinatorial effects of multiple targets can be predicted and used to explain the side effects of a drug.
a systems biology approach to the study of adverse drug reactions is possible, and that it is a promising approach to drug discovery and development.
the adverse side effects of a drug can be predicted from the drug-protein binding network, and that this network can be systematically constructed using the structural genomic data.
